facts.statement: Flexomornis is an extinct genus of enantiornithean bird found in the Woodbine Formation of Texas, dating to the middle Cenomanian age of the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Flexomornis (meaning "flexed shoulder bird") is an extinct genus of enantiornithean bird known from the Woodbine Formation (Lewisville Member) of Texas, United States, dating to the middle Cenomanian age of the late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The holotype of Flexomornis howei was discovered just 100 meters away from the holotype of Ampelognathus coheni.
facts.quote: The holotype of F. howei was found 100 m away from the holotype of Ampelognathus coheni.

facts.statement: Flexomornis is classified as a member of the extinct bird group Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: Flexomornis (meaning "flexed shoulder bird") is an extinct genus of enantiornithean bird

facts.statement: The parent group of Flexomornis is Enantiornithes.
Flexomornis is classified within the class Reptilia.
Flexomornis lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Flexomornis was described by Tykoski and Fiorillo in 2010.
The species name of the genus is howei.

rejected.statement: The only known species, Flexomornis howei, was named after amateur fossil hunter Kris Howe, who discovered the fossil site.
rejected.quote: It contains a single species, Flexomornis howei, named for the amateur fossil hunter Kris Howe, who discovered the site where the fossils were found.
